--- title: "Rapid automatized naming: varied long objects" subtitle: "Automatically generated task sheet · RAN_OBJETOS_VARIADOS_LARGOS" --- ::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"} **Automatically generated task sheet** (B · Rapid naming; quality class C). Generated on November 28, 2026 with `scripts/R/ficha_generica_v3.R --tarea RAN_OBJETOS_VARIADOS_LARGOS`. Figures come from the data; the theoretical framework is shared by the tasks of the same construct. **Interpretation and team review are missing.** Spanish name: *Denominación rápida de objetos variados (largos)*. [Spanish version](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/fichas/auto/RAN_OBJETOS_VARIADOS_LARGOS.html). ::: ::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple"} **Class C.** It was given to few children, at few time points or in different versions. The task sheet documents the task and its first data; figures are descriptive and cannot yet be used as norms. [What each class means](../../limites.en.qmd#sec-clases). ::: **In one sentence.** Rapid automatized naming: varied long objects, from age 4 to 8 (1,830 administrations in 3 cohorts). Stability across time points ρ = .45. AUC .67–.72 against persistent reading difficulty. ## Description | | | |---|---| | Codes | 1946 531 | | Battery | LEEDUCA and DIS-ESP | | Format | rapid naming of a series | | Items | — | | Task family | B · Rapid naming | | Score | Time (s; lower is better) | | Instructions (platform) | En la pantalla van a aparecer dibujos que el niño debe nombrar lo más rápido que pueda. Cuando la respuesta sea correcta, debes marcarlo con el botón izquierdo del ratón, cuando sea incorrecta con el derecho. *(Spanish)* | ![Example of the screen format (2018 screenshot; not necessarily an item from this task).](../../figuras/pantallas/formato_ran.png){width=45%} ## Theoretical framework Rapid naming of pictures measures how quickly the child retrieves and says, in series, very familiar names; it is one of the best predictors of reading fluency. The variants change: - the **phonological similarity** of the names: same initial syllable, same initial phoneme, or unrelated names (control); - the **length** of the names: short or long; - **repetition**: five repeated pictures or varied pictures, on a card or one at a time. **What the evidence says:** - **RAN predicts reading, also with pictures and before reading.** A meta-analysis of 137 studies (28,826 participants) finds a moderate to strong relation (r = .43). Stimulus type is one of the most influential moderators [@araujo2014ran]. In a three-year longitudinal study, non-alphanumeric RAN measured before reading instruction predicted fluency growth, with no reverse effect of reading on RAN [@lervag2009ran]. - **In Spanish, pictures and alphanumeric stimuli form distinct factors.** In 874 Spanish children from Grade 2 to Grade 6, RAN tasks group into an alphanumeric and a non-alphanumeric factor, stable across grades [@rodriguez2015ran]. - **Phonological similarity adds a load that affects dyslexia more, but with letters.** Readers with dyslexia are more impaired than others when adjacent letters sound similar [@jones2013ran]. We have not found studies that manipulate picture names in this way: this variant is specific to the platform and its interpretation is, for now, a hypothesis. - **Format matters.** In Grade 1, serial RAN is more strongly related to reading than discrete RAN (one stimulus at a time) [@dejong2011discrete]. **What our data show.** These are class B and C tasks, with few sessions per variant: - **Stability.** ρ = .33 (control), .42 (same syllable) and .41 (same phoneme) across terms from age 4 to 6; .45 for the long versions at ages 7 to 8. - **Validity.** Against persistent difficulty, AUC from .55 to .72 at ages 4 to 6 and from .57 to .74 at ages 7–8. Against later low comprehension, only .52 to .63. Against Woodcock-Muñoz, maximum AUC of .70. - **Phonological similarity.** The same-phoneme version reaches .72 at age 6, compared with .65–.67 for the control, but the intervals overlap: there is no clear advantage in manipulating phonology. - **Caution.** Mean times change a lot between sessions of the same school year (in the control version, 25.5 s at 4.1 and 44.5 s at 4.2). Norms must be computed by session and the administered version reviewed. ## Sample and descriptive statistics | Time point| Cohort| Session|School year | N| Non-Preleo| Preleo| Schools| |----------:|------:|-------:|:-----------|---:|----------:|------:|-------:| | 7.1| 2010| 184|2017/18 | 743| 231| 511| 31| | 7.2| 2012| 904|2019/20 | 190| 186| 0| 11| | 8.2| 2011| 905|2019/20 | 442| 0| 442| 22| | 8.3| 2010| 640|2018/19 | 455| 100| 354| 24| | Time point| N| Cohorts| Mean| SD| Median| Skewness|% floor |% ceiling | |----------:|---:|-------:|-----:|----:|------:|--------:|:-------|:---------| | 7.1| 231| 2010| 30.44| 8.55| 28.67| 1.08|NA |NA | | 7.2| 186| 2012| 32.88| 9.15| 32.27| 0.77|NA |NA | | 8.3| 100| 2010| 27.19| 7.69| 25.77| 1.31|NA |NA | **Score range** (non-Preleo group, in seconds). The usual range goes from P1 to P99 (98% of the children). The minimum–maximum is the one observed after cleaning. | Time point| N|Usual range (P1–P99) |Min.–max. | Warning| |----------:|---:|:--------------------|:---------|-------:| | 7.1| 231|16.3–58.5 |14.8–61.1 | | | 7.2| 186|19.2–59.5 |15.3–61.2 | | | 8.3| 100|16.1–48.6 |15.9–56.5 | | ## Reliability Stability across time points in the same children: ρ from .45 (median .45, 1 pairs of time points). Internal consistency from item-level responses is missing. As a timed task, stability is the preferred reliability estimate. | Cohort| From| To| n| r| ρ| |------:|----:|---:|---:|----:|----:| | 2010| 7.1| 8.3| 380| 0.41| 0.45| ## Validity **Concurrent.** With other tasks in its own domain (Rapid naming (RAN)), r = .32–.60. Outside its domain, the highest relation is with: Word and text reading (7.1, r = .31); Word and text reading (7.2, r = .34); Word and text reading (8.2, r = .40); Word and text reading (8.3, r = .47). **Against reading difficulty and comprehension.** Against persistent difficulty, AUC .67–.72. Against poor comprehension one or two school years later (non-circular criterion), AUC .58–.59. ![Validity: AUC with 95% confidence interval (labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_RAN_OBJETOS_VARIADOS_LARGOS_F2_validez.png){width=85%} **Against an external criterion, years later.** Against low Woodcock-Muñoz reading fluency in 2021/22 ([chapter](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/criterio-woodcock.html), *in Spanish*), AUC .59–.67 (3 time points; 226–315 children). ## Provisional norms | Time point| N| Cohorts| P5| P10| P16| P25| P50| P75| P90| |----------:|---:|-------:|----:|----:|----:|----:|----:|----:|----:| | 7.1| 231| 2010| 47.9| 42.7| 38.1| 34.6| 28.7| 24.5| 21.8| | 7.2| 186| 2012| 48.8| 46.2| 41.6| 37.8| 32.3| 25.7| 22.2| | 8.2| 442| 2011| 32.9| 29.5| 25.8| 24.1| 20.7| 17.7| 15.9| | 8.3| 100| 2010| 42.1| 36.0| 33.4| 31.1| 25.8| 21.6| 19.8| In rapid naming, less time is better: P10 is the time of the slowest 10%. These are norms by time point (school year × term). For dates between assessments and time points without a normative sample, study M3 proposes continuous norms on **months of instruction**, not on age, with relative age within the school year as an adjustment. ![Provisional norms (non-Preleo schools; labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_RAN_OBJETOS_VARIADOS_LARGOS_F1_baremo.png){width=85%} ## Variables that affect it |Variable | Time point| n| Effect| p| |:---------------------------------------|----------:|---:|------:|-----:| |School SES (ρ) | 7.1| 700| 0.173| 0.000| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 7.1| 743| -0.064| 0.387| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 7.1| 742| 0.001| 0.980| |School (ICC) | 7.1| 743| 0.052| | |School SES (ρ) | 7.2| 188| 0.047| 0.520| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 7.2| 190| 0.007| 0.961| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 7.2| 190| 0.067| 0.355| |School (ICC) | 7.2| 190| 0.042| | |School SES (ρ) | 8.2| 441| 0.023| 0.627| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 8.2| 442| -0.076| 0.430| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 8.2| 441| 0.008| 0.860| |School (ICC) | 8.2| 442| 0.088| | |School SES (ρ) | 8.3| 455| 0.099| 0.035| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 8.3| 448| -0.010| 0.916| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 8.3| 447| -0.006| 0.901| |School (ICC) | 8.3| 455| 0.063| | ## For publications The LEEDUCA platform task “Rapid automatized naming: varied long objects” (codes 1946 and 531; LEEDUCA and DIS-ESP battery) assesses rapid automatized naming (lexical access). The child names a series of familiar stimuli on the screen as quickly as possible, and the examiner records correct responses and errors. The time limit is 30 seconds. It is administered individually on a computer at school. In the 2010, 2011 and 2012 cohorts it was administered in 6 sessions, from 4 to 8 years of age. The main outcome is the completion time (seconds). Stability across time points was ρ = .45. Against later poor reading comprehension, AUC = .58–.59. ## Pending issues - The task has several codes (versions or forms): check that time points are comparable before pooling norms. - Write the interpretation; review with the team.
